E1.evidence: Reporter gives setup (Ubuntu 24.04, Jazzy binaries), a reproducer (install ros-jazzy-qml-ros2-plugin, which uses a .dsv environment hook) and the effect ("The variable is missing and based on my investigation .dsv environment hooks are generally not processed."); a maintainer confirms: "If it's working with a colcon workspace but not the ament workspace created by the debs, then it's almost certainly a bug." -- https://github.com/ros2/ros2/issues/1613

units_identified: ament_package (prefix-level setup script template _local_setup_util.py in the binary install space)
E2.evidence: The defect is in the workspace environment-setup machinery that packaging installs: ament_package's prefix_level/_local_setup_util.py only groups hook files with the shell's primary/additional extension, so a .dsv hook without a same-named .sh is ignored (ament_package issue #145: "`.dsv` files not processed properly unless there is a `.sh` file with the same name registered with `ament_environment_hooks`"). The resolving change is to that packaging template only: ament_package PR #147 "Always consider .dsv files, even when no shell specific script exists" (merge 01592eb7 on rolling, 2024-04-28), moving "basenames[path_without_ext] = set()" out of the extension check; the documented workaround is also packaging-level ("create a dummy `.sh` file with the same name as the `.dsv` file"). No ROS runtime interface (topic, service, action, parameter, message definition or library API) of any node changes; the only effect is an environment variable (QML2_IMPORT_PATH / GST_PLUGIN_PATH) not set when the install space is sourced. The packet's ros-gst-bridge PR #74 (merge ae6e2bf4) only adds a .dsv hook ("ament_environment_hooks(register_plugin.dsv.in)", "prepend-non-duplicate;GST_PLUGIN_PATH;lib/@PROJECT_NAME@/") and notes "This currently only works in source workspaces due to ros2/ros2#1613."

E4.evidence: "The variable is missing" after sourcing setup.bash with the binary package installed -- https://github.com/ros2/ros2/issues/1613
